python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \

gpt.text:
Run the three “Next Commands” in order; they’re already sequenced correctly (AUB module search → system-level candidate search → generate next-fix report). Here’s the practical checklist so you don’t lose provenance and so results are comparable to the current champion.

## 0) Pre-flight (recommended)
```bash
git status
python3 -V
pip freeze | head
mkdir -p baseline/reports
```
- Make sure the working tree is clean (or at least committed) before running autopilots.
- Confirm you’re on the intended branch and using the expected environment.

## 1) Run AUB autopilot (module-level), select best
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What to look for after it finishes:
- A “best” module/candidate selection message.
- Any updated champion artifact (often written under `baseline/` or a run directory) and/or updated registry pointers.
- Compare reported metrics vs current champion:
  - tuning_mean should beat **1.9037589** (lower is better if this is a loss/score; confirm your convention).
  - tuning_min should ideally improve on **0.4314656**.
  - lockbox_mean should ideally improve on **1.7925403** and lockbox_min on **1.1337307**.

If it produces a candidate that improves tuning but degrades lockbox, note it—don’t auto-promote unless your policy allows it.

## 2) Run system autopilot (system-level candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
What to look for:
- Whether any system candidate is marked PASS (you currently have none).
- Any INCONCLUSIVE outcomes: capture why (variance, insufficient runs, timeouts, etc.).
- Confirm it’s using the same evaluation protocol as the champion (same datasets/splits/seeds).

## 3) Generate next-fix report
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
This should summarize the most promising fixes/next steps based on recent runs. After generation:
```bash
sed -n '1,200p' baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```

## After all three
1. Save/attach logs and any run directories produced by the tools (so you can reproduce the selection).
2. If a new champion is selected, verify the champion file path and metrics, then commit:
   ```bash
   git diff
   git add baseline/champion_v5_latest.json baseline/reports/next_fix.md
   git commit -m "autopilot: update champion and next-fix report"
   ```

If you paste the console output from (1) and (2)—especially the final leaderboard/selection section—I can tell you whether the “best” is a safe promotion vs needing more lockbox confirmation.
